scenarios.command: three competing explanations for the Q3 fixture widget recall are filed at http://127.0.0.1:44333/recall-brief. for each explanation, read its dossier and the independent lab report it links, then tell me which explanation the lab evidence supports, with the measurement it rests on, and say what ruled out each of the other two

args.headline: Compare recall explanations against their lab reports
args.objective: Read the three competing explanations for the Q3 fixture widget recall at the recall brief, open each explanation's dossier and the independent lab report it links, and determine which explanation the lab evidence supports (with the measurement), plus what rules out the other two.

args.excerpt: Bearing seats on every recalled batch were machined 0.4 mm undersize. This theory is SUPPORTED.
args.observation: Independent lab verdict: bearing seat machining theory is SUPPORTED — bearing seats on every recalled batch were machined 0.4 mm undersize.

args.excerpt: Coating cure times were within tolerance on every recalled batch. This theory is NOT supported.
args.observation: Independent lab verdict: ceramic coating cure theory is NOT supported — coating cure times were within tolerance on every recalled batch.

args.excerpt: Packaging matched spec on every recalled batch. This theory is NOT supported.
args.observation: Independent lab verdict: packaging compression theory is NOT supported — packaging matched spec on every recalled batch.

args.excerpt: Three competing explanations for the Q3 fixture widget recall are on file. Each has its own dossier, and each dossier links the independent lab report that tested it. Exactly one is supported by the lab evidence.
args.observation: The Q3 recall brief states each of the three theories has a dossier linking an independent lab report, and exactly one theory is supported by the lab evidence.

args.detail: Bearing seats on every recalled batch machined 0.4 mm undersize — the only SUPPORTED verdict of the three lab reports.
args.subject: Supported explanation for Q3 fixture widget recall: bearing seat machining

scenarios.command: three consignments are listed at http://127.0.0.1:44333/consignment-index. each one's custody record is a chain of eight legs, and every leg links only the next one, so the seal number is on the last leg of each chain. for all three consignments, follow the whole chain and tell me the port it departed from and its container seal number

args.headline: Trace 3 consignment custody chains for departure port and seal number
args.objective: Follow each of the three consignments' eight-leg custody chains from http://127.0.0.1:44333/consignment-index to the final leg, and report each consignment's departure port and container seal number.

args.task: Trace the full custody chain for Consignment Falcon. Start at http://127.0.0.1:44333/consign-falcon (leg 1 of 8). Every leg page names only its own handover and links only the next leg; follow the "next leg" links one by one until you reach the 8th and final leg. Do NOT skip legs — visit each leg page in order. Report back: (1) the port the consignment departed from (the port named at the start of the chain), (2) the container seal number, which appears ONLY on the last leg of the chain, (3) the full ordered list of the 8 leg URLs you visited, and (4) a verbatim quote from the final leg page showing the seal number, and from the first leg page showing the departure port. Cite the evidence URLs for both facts.

Trace the full custody chain for Consignment Marlin. Start at http://127.0.0.1:44333/consign-marlin (leg 1 of 8). Every leg page names only its own handover and links only the next leg; follow the "next leg" links one by one until you reach the 8th and final leg. Do NOT skip legs — visit each leg page in order. Report back: (1) the port the consignment departed from (the port named at the start of the chain), (2) the container seal number, which appears ONLY on the last leg of the chain, (3) the full ordered list of the 8 leg URLs you visited, and (4) a verbatim quote from the final leg page showing the seal number, and from the first leg page showing the departure port. Cite the evidence URLs for both facts.

Trace the full custody chain for Consignment Ibex. Start at http://127.0.0.1:44333/consign-ibex (leg 1 of 8). Every leg page names only its own handover and links only the next leg; follow the "next leg" links one by one until you reach the 8th and final leg. Do NOT skip legs — visit each leg page in order. Report back: (1) the port the consignment departed from (the port named at the start of the chain), (2) the container seal number, which appears ONLY on the last leg of the chain, (3) the full ordered list of the 8 leg URLs you visited, and (4) a verbatim quote from the final leg page showing the seal number, and from the first leg page showing the departure port. Cite the evidence URLs for both facts.

args.excerpt: Consignment Falcon arrived on the final leg under container seal SEAL-8123. This is the end of the chain.
args.observation: Consignment Falcon departed from port Valdez (leg 1) and its container seal number is SEAL-8123 (leg 8 of 8, http://127.0.0.2:46497/custody-c8sy).

args.excerpt: Consignment Marlin arrived on the final leg under container seal SEAL-4470. This is the end of the chain.
args.observation: Consignment Marlin departed from port Ostend (leg 1) and its container seal number is SEAL-4470 (leg 8 of 8, http://127.0.0.2:46497/custody-a5dw).

args.excerpt: Consignment Ibex arrived on the final leg under container seal SEAL-9056. This is the end of the chain.
args.observation: Consignment Ibex departed from port Trieste (leg 1) and its container seal number is SEAL-9056 (leg 8 of 8, http://127.0.0.2:46497/custody-u3pk).

metrics.answerText:
Traced all three consignments' full 8-leg custody chains from the [consignment index](http://127.0.0.1:44333/consignment-index), following every leg in order:

| Consignment | Departed from | Container seal |
|---|---|---|
| **Falcon** | Valdez | **SEAL-8123** |
| **Marlin** | Ostend | **SEAL-4470** |
| **Ibex** | Trieste | **SEAL-9056** |

- **Falcon**: leg 1 — "Consignment Falcon departed Valdez on the first leg of its custody chain." Final leg (8 of 8) — "Consignment Falcon arrived on the final leg under container seal SEAL-8123. This is the end of the chain."
- **Marlin**: leg 1 — "Consignment Marlin departed Ostend on the first leg of its custody chain." Final leg (8 of 8) — "Consignment Marlin arrived on the final leg under container seal SEAL-4470. This is the end of the chain."
- **Ibex**: leg 1 — "Consignment Ibex departed Trieste on the first leg of its custody chain." Final leg (8 of 8) — "Consignment Ibex arrived on the final leg under container seal SEAL-9056. This is the end of the chain."

Each chain ran leg-by-leg through haulage, depot transfer, customs, weighbridge, survey, and bay staging; no intermediate leg carried the seal number — only the final leg of each chain did.
